Contributing to graphlearnR

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution to graphlearnR. The package brings graph machine learning and graph neural networks to R on top of torch. A change is judged on whether it is numerically correct, whether it keeps the graph semantics the package documents, and whether it fits R conventions.

Before You Start

  • Use GitHub issues for bug reports, feature requests, and documentation gaps.
  • For a new layer, task, or dataset, open an issue first so the design can be discussed before implementation.
  • Keep pull requests focused. A new layer, a bug fix, and a refactor should usually be separate pull requests.

Development Setup

install.packages(c("remotes", "devtools", "roxygen2", "testthat"))
remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)
torch::install_torch()

Tests that need LibTorch skip when it is not installed. Tests that need a GPU skip when no CUDA or MPS device is available.

Package Rules

  • Node indices are 1-based in every public interface: edge_index, seeds, pairs, masks, and sampled node ids. Convert to 0-based only through to_zero_based() at an explicit boundary.
  • An undirected graph is given with one entry per pair and stored in both directions. Code that counts, splits, or samples edges must respect edge_pair.
  • Splits must not leak. A held out link must not appear in the message passing graph of any training step, nor in a reverse relation of a heterogeneous graph. Temporal code must only use events strictly before the query time.
  • New layers need a permutation equivariance test, a comparison with a dense or reference formula, and a finite difference gradient check in double precision.
  • Reproducibility: functions that draw random numbers take a seed argument and must not change the caller’s R random number state.
  • Do not add performance claims without a benchmark script under benchmarks/ and recorded hardware details.
  • Do not bundle third party datasets unless their license allows redistribution. Download them with checksum verification instead.

Branches and Pull Requests

  • Use one branch per logical change, named after the change (add-cheb-conv, fix-negative-sampling-bipartite).
  • Write commit subjects in the imperative (“Add Chebyshev spectral convolution”).
  • Keep the implementation, its tests, the roxygen source, the regenerated man/ pages, and a NEWS entry in the same pull request.
  • Continuous integration runs R CMD check on Linux, macOS, and Windows. A pull request is ready to merge when the checks pass.

Code of Conduct

Please note that this project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By participating you agree to abide by its terms.
